Dated this the 10th day of September, 2024 Crl.M.C. No.1729/2024 has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking to quash proceedings in C.C. No.204/2017 pending before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Aluva, arising out of Crime No.839/2016 of Edathala Police Station, Ernakulam and the petitioner is the 2 nd accused.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Accused Nos.3 and 4 in the same crime are the petitioners in Crl.M.C. No.215/2024 and they also seek quashment as prayed for by the 2nd accused.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned counsel for the defacto complainant and the learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the records including the statements, which form part of the case diary placed by the learned Public Prosecutor.
Here the prosecution alleges commission of offences punishable under Section 498A read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code by accused Nos.1 to 4.

The 1 st accused is the husband of the defacto complainant, the 2nd accused is the brother of the 1st accused and accused Nos.3 and 4 are the Naufal Abdul Kareem vs State Of Kerala on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56733467/
3 parents of the 1st accused.

sentences.text: 5. While canvassing quashment sought for, the learned counsel for the petitioners read out the FIS given by the defacto complainant as well as the 161 statement of her father, contending that only vague and omnibus allegations raised against the petitioners seeking quashment of the proceedings with a view to obtain the residential house purchased by the 2 nd accused in Combara, where the marriage function took place.

6. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, in the statement given by the defacto complainant, entrustment of Rs.15 lakh at the hands of the 2 nd accused at the 2024:KER:69520 CRL.MC Nos. 215 & 1729 of 2024 time of fixation of the marriage, is the allegation.
That apart, it is alleged that the 2nd accused also persecuted the defacto complainant at the time when he would be available in native place.

He also pointed that in the statement given by the father of the defacto complainant, Ayoob Khan, it was stated that Rs.15 lakh was entrusted at the date of fixation of marriage on 26.07.2015 and the same was received and counted by the 2 nd accused.
The learned counsel would submit further that there are only remote allegations against the other accused also.
Therefore, quashment sought for is liable to be allowed.

7. While opposing quashment, the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent would submit that, on reading the prosecution records, including the statements of the defacto complainant and the other witnesses, the involvement of the petitioners herein in this crime by misusing the money belonged to the defacto complainant and cruelty at their volition could be 2024:KER:69520 CRL.MC Nos. 215 & 1729 of 2024 gathered.
Therefore, quashment is liable to fail.
8. The learned Public Prosecutor also read out the FIS and witness statements while opposing quashment on the submission that prima facie case made against the petitioners.
9. On perusal of the FIS, it could be gathered that entrustment of Rs.15 lakh at the hands of the 2 nd accused at the time of fixation of the marriage, is the main allegation.
That apart, there is allegation that the 2nd accused also persecuted the defacto complainant at the time when he would be available in native place.

In the statement given by the father of the defacto complainant, Ayoob Khan, it was stated that Rs.15 lakh was entrusted at the date of fixation of marriage on 26.07.2015 and the same was received and counted by the 2 nd accused.

But there are allegations of cruelty specifically stated against accused Nos.3 and 4 and at this juncture, the learned counsel for the petitioners fairly submitted that they are ready to face trial and 2024:KER:69520 CRL.MC Nos. 215 & 1729 of 2024 quashment sought against them can be closed.
However, he pressed for quashment of the case as against the 2 nd accused for want of materials.

10. In order to address the rival contentions, reference to Section 498A of IPC is necessary, which reads as under:
"Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty - Whoever,
being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three Naufal Abdul Kareem vs State Of Kerala on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56733467/
4 years and shall also be liable to fine.

entities.text: Naufal Abdul Kareem vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Explanation.--For the purposes of this section,
"cruelty means"--
(a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or 2024:KER:69520 CRL.MC Nos. 215 & 1729 of 2024 (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."
Going by the definition, subjecting a woman to cruelty by husband or relative of the husband likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman or harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coerce her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand is an offence.

In the decision in Achin Gupta v. State of Haryana's case (supra), the Apex Court considered earlier decisions of the Apex Court dealing with Section 498A of IPC and it was held that general and sweeping allegations without 2024:KER:69520 CRL.MC Nos. 215 & 1729 of 2024 mentioning specific instances of criminal conduct is an abuse of the process of court and in such cases the courts owe a duty to subject the allegations levelled in the complaint to a thorough scrutiny to find out, prima facie, whether there is any grain of truth in the allegations or whether they are made only with the sole object of involving some individuals in a criminal charge, more particularly, when a prosecution arises from a matrimonial dispute.
11. Going by the allegation raised against the 2 nd accused, the allegation is merely that he received Rs.15 lakh at the time of marriage fixation and counted.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, he also subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty along with others while he was available in the native place.
In fact, no specific allegation raised against the 2nd accused to show prima facie that he has committed the offences alleged.

Therefore, his inclusion in the final report and further proceedings against him are liable to 2024:KER:69520 CRL.MC Nos. 215 & 1729 of 2024 be quashed, while allowing the prosecution to continue as against the other accused persons.

In the result, Crl.M.C. No.1729/2024 stands allowed and further proceedings in C.C. No.204/2017 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Aluva stands quashed as against the 2nd accused.
